messages:
Matt O.: FYI — Azure sent an updated commitment term. Main change: GPU credits get 'smoothing' over 90 days and are reconciled per-region. Link to term sheet (redacted): https://vendor.redacted/edp-terms
Lauren (Azure Rep): We're proposing smoothing to reduce month-to-month invoice swings. The idea is credits are earned immediately but applied on a 90d rolling basis to even out billing. Also proposing a regional reconciliation on the 1st of each month.
Jules R.: Can you paste a sample invoice we can model? need to know how they surface the credit lines.
Ibrahim K.: Reproduced based on their example — minimal invoice excerpt below to show mechanics:
```
INVOICE 2026-02
SKU: GPU_V100_HOURS  qty: 1000  unit_price: $3.20  line_total: $3,200.00
SKU: GPU_COMMIT_CREDIT  applied: -$1,200.00  description: 90d-smoothed credit
ADJUSTMENT: regional true-up (applied later)
TOTAL DUE: $2,000.00
```
Ibrahim K.: Practically, smoothing delays ~40% of credit impact into later months for the first 90d window. For our bursty usage that increases effective unit cost in month 1 by ~14% in this toy model.
Jules R.: Not great. Can legal/procurement push back to have committed credits apply at invoice time and then true-up quarterly? That keeps short-term cashflow predictable.
Maggie L.: Draft counter language: "Committed GPU credits shall be applied against monthly invoices at the time of charge. Any periodic true-ups shall be limited to quarterly reconciliations, disclosed 30 days in advance, and shall not exceed +/-5% variation per billing period without Customer consent." Also request that regional reallocations require written approval.
Lauren (Azure Rep): I can try to sell that. Vendor finance is worried about volatility from customers who churn. Would a hybrid help: immediate application up to a committed floor, with smoothing only applied to incremental overage credits?
Matt O.: Hybrid seems pragmatic. Also need a hard carveout: provider cannot reclassify reserved GPUs into preemptible/spot without 60 days notice and our explicit consent. We need the reserved pool guaranteed per-region in writing.
Jules R.: Agreed. Ibrahim, can you run the billing model comparing vendor smoothing vs hybrid vs immediate-apply? 12-month horizon please.
Ibrahim K.: On it. Quick parser snippet I'm running against last year's invoices: 
```bash
python tools/parse_invoices.py --samples invoices/2025-* --apply-smoothing 90 --compare hybrid immediate
```
billing-bot: invoice parser job queued (job-4421)
Ibrahim K.: Preliminary: hybrid reduces month-1 delta to ~2.3% vs prior policy (vs 14% for full smoothing). Annualized cashflow difference under hybrid is <3% for our current profile.
Jules R.: If those numbers hold, finance is comfortable with hybrid plus a strict regional guarantee and a penalty credit if provider moves >10% of committed pool out of region without notice.
Maggie L.: I'll draft a penalty-credit clause: "Provider to maintain committed GPU pool per region within +/-5%; breaches will trigger a credit equal to 5x the daily rate for the shortfall for each day beyond the remediation window." We can negotiate the multiplier but need teeth.
Lauren (Azure Rep): Noted. I'll push hybrid + regional guarantee + proposed penalty to our finance team and see what they accept. Will get a revised term sheet back by EOD Thursday.
Matt O.: Thanks. Our negotiation asks: 1) immediate application up to floor, smoothing only on overage; 2) explicit per-region reserved pool not subject to preemption; 3) clear true-up cadence (quarterly) and advance notice; 4) penalty credits for region breaches. If Lauren can get those in writing and hybrid keeps delta <5%, we'll sign. :thumbsup:
Jules R.: I'll stand by to model final numbers and approve.
Lauren (Azure Rep): I'll loop finance and legal and return with a redline.
Matt O.: Great — please cc procurement and ops when you send the redline. Thanks all.
